audit.title: Data Sources

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong lead: "Chainlink Data Streams source pricing data from multiple independent aggregators and vendors across asset classes." Self-contained and liftable; the table stands alone. Minor: the `<DataStreams section="dsNotes" />` component renders nothing in the served markdown, so any notes it carries are invisible to engines.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: One H1, one coherent table, no level skips. Fine for a page this size, but a single 155-word section with no H2 subheadings limits multi-question retrievability.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Has some numerics ("3+", "Single source from 1") but 0 carry units and none name actual providers or stream counts. "3+ market data vendors" is vaguer than it needs to be.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Weak: 2 links, none to primary/methodology sources. Claims about aggregation and CEX/DEX sourcing are unattributed.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: "Data Streams," "LWBA," "Crypto State Price," and "Data Link Long Tail" lack crisp standalone definitions; LWBA is expanded inline only within a table cell.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weakest dimension: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags, no head metadata captured. Nothing signals freshness or entity identity to an agent.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, and none is needed for this conceptual page; scored neutral, not penalized.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Answers "where does Data Streams get its data?" well but nothing else — no per-asset FAQ phrasing, no "is Forex data reliable?", no methodology questions.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clean, unambiguous, consistent product naming. Strong; no action needed.

audit.summary: This is a short, single-table reference page describing where Chainlink Data Streams sources its market data by asset class. Its strength is a clean, liftable summary table with an answer-first lead sentence; its biggest weaknesses are near-absent machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, no canonical, no dates) and thin query coverage — the page answers exactly one implied question and offers no symptom- or intent-phrased headings that would win retrieval. The honest verdict: solid bones, but too thin and metadata-poor to be reliably retrieved and cited as-is.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/intent-phrased headings
recommendations.where: Under the H1, before the table.
recommendations.issue: Only one heading ("Data Sources"); concept-titled, not question-titled.
recommendations.change: Add H2s such as "Where does Chainlink Data Streams source crypto prices?", "How is Forex / Precious Metals / US Equities data sourced?", and "What is Crypto LWBA vs Crypto State Price?" placing the table row's answer as the first sentence under each.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by asset and question, not by the abstract label "Data Sources"; question-phrased headings win retrieval this page currently loses.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `about` (Chainlink Data Streams), canonical URL `https://docs.chain.link/data-streams/data-sources`, and a visible `dateModified`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and a freshness signal raise parse-trust and citation likelihood; their absence is a measured, fixable defect.

recommendations.title: Define the canonical terms inline
recommendations.issue: "Crypto LWBA", "Crypto State Price", "Data Link Long Tail Crypto" used without standalone definitions.
recommendations.change: Add one crisp sentence per term, e.g. "LWBA (Liquidity-Weighted Bid/Ask) reports bid, ask, and mid prices weighted by orderbook liquidity from CEX data."
recommendations.why: Verbatim-liftable definitions near first use outperform diffuse table-cell expansions.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative references
recommendations.where: After the intro sentence and in the note block.
recommendations.issue: Sourcing claims (CEX orderbook, DEX pool state) are unattributed; only link is a contact form.
recommendations.change: Link to the Data Streams overview, feed/stream ID reference, and any published data-provider/methodology page.
recommendations.why: Inline primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate for the sourcing claims.

recommendations.title: Sharpen specifics
recommendations.change: Where disclosable, state the number of independent sources per asset class or link to the live stream count; add "as of {date}".
recommendations.why: Quantitative, dated specifics are among the highest-lift changes for generative visibility.

recommendations.title: Surface the hidden component content
recommendations.issue: Renders empty in served markdown; any caveats are invisible to engines.
recommendations.change: Ensure the component's notes render as static text server-side, or inline the key notes.
recommendations.why: Content only in an unrendered component cannot be retrieved or cited.

antiPatterns: Thin/undifferentiated content: the entire page is 158 words and one table — borderline too sparse to be a reliable citation target.
Undated content: no visible last-updated signal for time-sensitive sourcing claims.
Unrendered component (`dsNotes`) hides potential content from crawlers.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced — good; verify this page is listed in it and in the sitemap.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical defaults may exist but "could not be verified" here — the CLI should pass raw `<head>` for a definitive read.
Consider internal links from the Data Streams overview and feed-reference hub into this page (canonical-hub pattern) to improve its retrieval odds.
